**2.1 Introduction**

This policy establishes the framework for the disbursement of grant funds to approved beneficiaries under the Community Impact Fund (CIF). It applies to all grant agreements executed on or after the effective date of this version. The policy is intended to ensure timely, accurate, and accountable disbursement of funds while minimising risk to the Fund.

**2.2 Definitions**

For the purposes of this policy:

- **Beneficiary** – The organisation or individual receiving grant funds.
- **Disbursement** – The release of grant funds to a beneficiary.
- **Tier 1 Grant** – Grants up to S$50,000.
- **Tier 2 Grant** – Grants above S$50,000 and up to S$200,000.
- **Tier 3 Grant** – Grants above S$200,000.
- **Working Day** – Any day other than a Saturday, Sunday, or public holiday in Singapore.

**2.3 Disbursement Process**

The disbursement process shall follow the steps below:

1. The Grants Manager shall verify that all conditions precedent in the grant agreement have been fulfilled.
2. The beneficiary shall submit a disbursement request using the prescribed form (Form CIF-D1).
3. The Grants Manager shall review the request for completeness and accuracy.
4. For Tier 1 and Tier 2 grants, the Grants Manager may approve the disbursement.
5. For Tier 3 grants, the disbursement requires the approval of the Executive Director.
6. Payment shall be made via bank transfer to the beneficiary's designated account within ten (10) working days of approval.

The following new section (Section 6) has been introduced in v3 to address circumstances under which disbursement may be suspended:

> 6.1 The Grants Manager may suspend further disbursement under a grant agreement where there is reasonable cause to believe that:
> (a) grant funds have been misapplied; or
> (b) the grantee has failed to comply with any condition of the grant agreement; or
> (c) the grantee has provided false or misleading information in any report or declaration submitted under this policy.
>
> 6.2 Where disbursement is suspended, the Grants Manager shall notify the grantee in writing, stating the grounds for suspension and the steps required to remedy the issue.
>
> 6.3 The grantee may submit a written representation within 14 working days of the suspension notice. The Grants Manager shall consider the representation and respond within 10 working days.
>
> 6.4 Where the suspension is lifted, disbursement shall resume in accordance with the original schedule, unless otherwise agreed in writing. Where the suspension is upheld, the matter shall be referred to the Grant Review Committee for a final decision.

**3.4 New Section: Overpayment Recovery**

Section 7 addresses recovery of overpayments made to grantees:

> 7.1 Where it is determined that a grantee has received an overpayment, the grantee shall repay the overpaid amount within 30 days of written notice.

> 7.2 The Grants Manager may agree to a repayment schedule where the overpayment exceeds SGD 10,000 and the grantee demonstrates financial hardship. Repayment schedules shall not exceed 12 months unless approved by the Grant Review Committee.

**2. GRANT DISBURSEMENT POLICY v2 – DRAFT FOR REVIEW (19 Sep 2023)**

**Document ID:** GDP-v2-Draft-RevA
**Status at time of writing:** [SUPERSEDED] – Draft version, superseded by GDP-v2.1 and subsequently GDP-v3.
**Prepared by:** Marcus Lee, Grants Manager
**Date:** 19 September 2023

**2.1 Introduction**

This policy establishes the framework for the disbursement of grant funds to approved beneficiaries under the Community Impact Fund (CIF). It applies to all grant agreements executed on or after the effective date of this version. The policy is intended to ensure timely, accurate, and accountable disbursement of funds while minimising risk to the Fund.

**2.2 Definitions**

For the purposes of this policy:

- **Beneficiary** – The organisation or individual receiving grant funds.
- **Disbursement** – The release of grant funds to a beneficiary.
- **Tier 1 Grant** – Grants up to S$50,000.
- **Tier 2 Grant** – Grants above S$50,000 and up to S$200,000.
- **Tier 3 Grant** – Grants above S$200,000.
- **Working Day** – Any day other than a Saturday, Sunday, or public holiday in Singapore.

**2.3 Disbursement Process**

The disbursement process shall follow the steps below:

1. The Grants Manager shall verify that all conditions precedent in the grant agreement have been fulfilled.
2. The beneficiary shall submit a disbursement request using the prescribed form (Form CIF-D1).
3. The Grants Manager shall review the request for completeness and accuracy.
4. For Tier 1 and Tier 2 grants, the Grants Manager may approve the disbursement.
5. For Tier 3 grants, the disbursement requires the approval of the Executive Director.
6. Payment shall be made via bank transfer to the beneficiary's designated account within ten (10) working days of approval.

**2.4 Eligibility for Part-Time Workers**

Section 4 of this policy addresses the eligibility of part-time workers under grant-funded programmes. This section was the subject of significant review during the drafting of this version. The policy as drafted in this version reads as follows:

> 4.1 Part-time workers engaged in grant-funded activities are eligible for support under this policy, subject to the conditions in 4.2.
>
> 4.2 The conditions are: (a) the worker is engaged on a contract of service; (b) the work performed is directly attributable to the grant-funded project; and (c) the worker's hours are recorded and verifiable.

**Reviewer Comment (Inline, Section 4):**

The following comment was recorded on this draft version, specifically on Section 4:

> **Comment by Marcus Lee (Grants Manager), dated 25 Sep 2023:** Need to clarify eligibility for part-time workers.

This comment was noted during the review cycle and was carried forward to the next revision of the policy. The comment reflects the need for greater specificity regarding the minimum hours of work, the treatment of casual workers, and whether part-time workers are eligible for the full range of support or only a pro-rated amount.

**2.5 Tiered Disbursement for Large Grants**

For Tier 3 grants, the policy introduces a milestone-based disbursement schedule. The schedule shall be agreed upon at the point of grant award and shall be documented in the grant agreement. The default schedule is as follows:

| Milestone | Percentage of Total Grant | Conditions for Release |
|-----------|---------------------------|------------------------|
| 1 | 30% | Upon execution of grant agreement |
| 2 | 40% | Upon submission and acceptance of interim progress report |
| 3 | 30% | Upon submission and acceptance of final report and financial statement |

In response to the comment recorded on 25 Sep 2023 regarding the need to clarify eligibility for part-time workers, Section 4 has been redrafted as follows:

**3.2 Tiered Disbursement for Large Grants (Revised Section 5)**

Section 5 of GDP-v3 retains the milestone-based disbursement schedule for Tier 3 grants, with the following amendments:

| Milestone | Percentage of Total Grant | Conditions for Release |
|-----------|---------------------------|------------------------|
| 1 | 30% | Upon execution of grant agreement |
| 2 | 40% | Upon submission and acceptance of interim progress report |
| 3 | 30% | Upon submission and acceptance of final report and financial statement |

Amendment A: For milestone 2, the interim progress report must include a certified statement of expenditure from the grantee's finance officer. This certification requirement was added in v3.

Amendment B: For milestone 3, the final report must be submitted no later than 90 days after the project end date. The grantee may apply for a single extension of up to 30 days, subject to written approval by the Grants Manager.

Amendment C: Where the grantee is a non-profit organisation with annual expenditure below SGD 500,000, the certification requirement in Amendment A may be substituted with a declaration signed by the organisation's board chairperson. This substitution is subject to review by the Grants Manager on a case-by-case basis.

**3.3 New Section: Disbursement Suspension and Reinstatement**

David Wong approval_of_grant_disbursement_policy_v3 is approved_with_conditions as per the review committee. Record status: current.

The following new section (Section 6) has been introduced in v3 to address circumstances under which disbursement may be suspended:

> 6.1 The Grants Manager may suspend further disbursement under a grant agreement where there is reasonable cause to believe that:
> (a) grant funds have been misapplied; or
> (b) the grantee has failed to comply with any condition of the grant agreement; or
> (c) the grantee has provided false or misleading information in any report or declaration submitted under this policy.
>
> 6.2 Where disbursement is suspended, the Grants Manager shall notify the grantee in writing, stating the grounds for suspension and the steps required to remedy the issue.
>
> 6.3 The grantee may submit a written representation within 14 working days of the suspension notice. The Grants Manager shall consider the representation and respond within 10 working days.
>
> 6.4 Where the suspension is lifted, disbursement shall resume in accordance with the original schedule, unless otherwise agreed in writing. Where the suspension is upheld, the matter shall be referred to the Grant Review Committee for a final decision.

**3.4 New Section: Overpayment Recovery**

Section 7 addresses recovery of overpayments made to grantees:

> 7.1 Where it is determined that a grantee has received an overpayment, the grantee shall repay the overpaid amount within 30 days of written notice.
>
> 7.2 The Grants Manager may agree to a repayment schedule where the overpayment exceeds SGD 10,000 and the grantee demonstrates financial hardship. Repayment schedules shall not exceed 12 months unless approved by the Grant Review Committee.
>
> 7.3 Interest shall not be charged on overpayments recovered under this section, provided the grantee complies with the repayment schedule. Where the grantee fails to comply, interest at the prevailing rate for late payment of government debts shall apply from the date of default.

**8. Implementation Notes – 15 Apr 2024**

Implementation of GDP-v3 proceeded as scheduled on 1 Apr 2024. The following operational notes were recorded by the Grants Operations team during the first two weeks of implementation.

| Item | Note |
|------|------|
| System update | Grant management system updated with new eligibility rules and appeal timeline on 31 Mar 2024. |
| Form revision | Appeal form (Form G-7) revised to reflect 20-working-day timeline. Old forms with 15-day reference withdrawn. |
| Suspension clause | New sub-clause 6.1(d) activated in system workflow. Grantee investigation flag added to case management screen. |
| Interest rate | Late payment interest rate linked to prevailing Ministry of Finance rate. System auto-calculates. |

No major issues reported. Two minor clarifications were requested by field officers regarding the interpretation of Section 2.1 for non-registered charities; these were addressed in a circular issued on 9 Apr 2024.

---

**8.1 Training on Policy Changes – 22 Apr 2024**

Two training sessions were conducted for staff on the changes introduced in GDP-v3.

- Session 1: 16 Apr 2024, 10:00–12:00, for Grants Officers and Programme Executives. Attended by 24 staff.
- Session 2: 18 Apr 2024, 14:00–16:00, for Finance and Compliance teams. Attended by 11 staff.

Training materials included a summary of key changes, case examples for the suspension clause, and a quick-reference card for the appeal timeline. Attendance records are filed under `Training/2024/GDP-v3/`.

Feedback forms were distributed at the end of each session. A summary of responses is included in Section 8.3 below.

---

**8.2 Feedback Forms – 25 Apr 2024**

A standard feedback form was used for both sessions. The form asked participants to rate the clarity of the training, the usefulness of the materials, and whether they felt confident applying the new policy. A total of 32 forms were returned (out of 35 attendees).

Ratings were on a scale of 1 (poor) to 5 (excellent).

| Question | Average Rating |
|----------|----------------|
| Clarity of training | 4.3 |
| Usefulness of materials | 4.1 |
| Confidence in applying policy | 3.9 |

Written comments were generally positive. A few participants noted that the suspension clause was complex and requested additional examples. This feedback was noted for future training sessions.

---

**8.3 Policy Implementation Notes – 30 Apr 2024**

The following implementation notes were compiled by the Grants Manager for the record.

- All active grants as of 1 Apr 2024 were reviewed against the new eligibility criteria. No existing grants were found to be non-compliant.
- The appeal timeline extension applies to appeals received on or after 1 Apr 2024. Appeals received before that date continue to follow the 15-working-day timeline.
- The suspension clause is being applied conservatively. As of 30 Apr 2024, no suspensions have been issued under sub-clause 6.1(d).
- Interest on late payments is calculated from the invoice due date. The applicable rate is the prevailing rate published by the Ministry of Finance, updated quarterly.
